sentences: Meningitis is the inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively known as the meninges
It is primarily caused by bacterial, viral, or fungal infections
The most common bacterial pathogens include Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae
The disease can lead to significant morbidity and mortality, especially if not treated promptly
Bacterial Meningitis: The most severe form, often caused by Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae
Viral Meningitis: Commonly less severe and caused by enteroviruses, herpes simplex virus, and other viruses
Fungal Meningitis: Less common and usually occurs in immunocompromised individuals; common culprits include Cryptococcus neoformans
Symptoms of meningitis include sudden onset of fever, headache, and stiff neck
Other symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), and altered mental status
Meningitis affects millions globally, with bacterial meningitis accounting for significant mortality
In 2017, there were approximately 10.6 million cases of meningitis worldwide, resulting in 288,000 deaths
Vaccination is a key preventive measure
Meningococcal vaccines (MenACWY and MenB) are recommended, especially for travelers to high-risk areas and specific age groups
Early diagnosis and treatment are critical
Empirical antibiotic therapy is usually initiated before the causative organism is identified
Common antibiotics include ceftriaxone and vancomycin
Prompt treatment significantly lowers the risk of complications and mortality
With appropriate treatment, the risk of death in bacterial meningitis is less than 15%
However, the prognosis varies depending on the causative organism and the patient’s age and overall health
